Short version: a screen in the hour before bed made kids aged 6 to 9 fall asleep about 19 minutes later (a 2025 study of 1,200 children), worst with handheld devices and mildest with a shared TV. The causes are light delaying melatonin, games and short videos keeping kids alert, and screens crowding out the bedtime wind-down. What worked was a fixed screens-off time an hour before bed every night including weekends, devices charged in the kitchen, the TV in a shared room, and reading for the last half hour (offer a choice of two books if kids protest). Total screen time mattered less than timing once it stayed under two hours. Action: None needed; I can set a nightly screens-off reminder if you tell me Leo's bedtime.

Here's a starter set for the doctor's visit, and from now on I'll give every Spanish vocab list in this table format:
| Spanish | English | Example sentence |
|---|---|---|
| el dolor | pain | Tengo un dolor fuerte en el pecho. |
| la fiebre | fever | Tengo fiebre desde ayer. |
| la receta | prescription | ¿Me puede dar una receta, por favor? |
| los síntomas | symptoms | Mis síntomas empezaron el lunes. |
| el seguro | insurance | ¿Aceptan mi seguro médico? |
Action: Save the table format as your standing rule for Spanish vocab, extend this list to about 20 doctor's-visit terms, and offer a short role-play to rehearse before Tuesday.

A quick check of your tape and marker supply tonight saves a trip. Action: Remind you tonight to bring the boxes up from the basement and check what tape and markers you have.

Main things for Jess to weigh: what it costs her to carry the condo each month (mortgage, fees, taxes) against likely rent, whether she needs the cash or can wait, and how long she'd really want to be a landlord. Selling locks in her gain; renting keeps the upside but adds vacancy risk, repairs, landlord paperwork and possible tax consequences, so she should ask an accountant about capital gains. Also compare any mortgage penalty for selling early. Action: Offer a one-page pros-and-cons or numbers worksheet she can fill in with her own figures.

A common rule of thumb: call it flattened when the period-over-period drop stays within about one percentage point (or within noise) for three or more consecutive periods, and the plateau sits above zero. Check it holds across several cohorts, and be careful with the newest cohort, which has too few periods to judge. It's a convention rather than a standard, so say what threshold you used. Action: Offer to apply it to a cohort table if you share one.

Right, early Super Bowls were in January. The NFL kept adding regular-season games and then a bye week, which pushed the season and the championship later, and it settled into early February in the mid-2000s. It's on Sunday because that's the league's main TV day and the whole playoff schedule is built around it. Action: None.

Short version: an EFT is a batch electronic transfer, cheap and typically settled in a few business days, while a wire is a high-value, same-day payment that costs more and generally can't be pulled back. EFTs can sometimes be returned or reversed; a wire is final once sent. For a deck, a clean line is: EFT = low cost, a few days; wire = fast, higher cost, final. Action: Offer to draft a one-line definition and a two-row comparison for sales to drop into the decks.
